text:
The largest recorded tree-cover loss event on this property was in 2020, at about 67.7 ha (Hansen Global Forest Change data). Earlier events were 25.5 ha in 2015, 4.8 ha in 2017 and 0.8 ha in 2008.

Two caveats:
- The 2020 event falls before the 2020-12-31 baseline, so it is historical and outside the 2021–2025 assessment window.
- Within 2021–2025, no loss event of 0.5 ha or more was detected, though about 0.4 ha of scattered small-patch loss appeared in 2021. This is below the event threshold and was not counted.

The analysis cannot rule out changes smaller than 0.5 ha or narrower than the 30 m pixels. It also makes no compliance finding, and it says nothing about periods outside those evaluated.

One oddity: the 2020 loss (67.7 ha) exceeds the 23 ha of tree cover recorded for 2000. Hansen loss is not limited to the 2000 baseline, so this doesn't necessarily indicate an error, but the tool output doesn't explain it.
